app_info.subtitle: Convert, save and share docs
app_info.description: Convert Markdown to HTML, Confluence, Jira or Slack markup, and HTML, CSV, JSON, plain text, RTF or Evernote exports to Markdown. With a connected TransformPipe account, save, search and read documents, organise them in folders, view versions and summaries, and share documents or folders. Publishing, emailing share notices and deleting ask for confirmation first. Binary files such as Word or PDF are not accepted through these tools.

justifications.read_only_justification: It searches the documentation text bundled with the server and returns matching sections; it reads and writes no account data, and like every tool call it is counted only for rate limiting.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only TransformPipe's own bundled documentation and FAQ; it fetches no URL and contacts no third party or person.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: nothing is created, changed, deleted or sent.
justifications.idempotent_justification: The same question returns the same sections, and a repeat changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It converts the Markdown supplied in the call to HTML, Confluence storage format, Jira wiki markup or Slack mrkdwn and returns it; nothing is saved to the account.
justifications.open_world_justification: The conversion runs locally on the server; it does not publish the result, fetch URLs found in the text, or call any third-party service.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: nothing is created, changed, deleted or sent.
justifications.idempotent_justification: A repeat has no effect beyond returning the conversion again; only the generation timestamp embedded in a standalone HTML page can differ.

justifications.read_only_justification: It converts HTML, CSV, TSV, JSON, plain text, RTF or ENEX text supplied in the call to Markdown and returns it without saving anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: It processes only the text passed in, with local converters; it never fetches URLs or images referenced in that text and contacts no one.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: nothing is created, changed, deleted or sent.
justifications.idempotent_justification: The same input returns the same Markdown, and a repeat changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates a new document in the connected account, plus any folders missing from the given folder path.
justifications.open_world_justification: share=link publishes a page anyone with the URL can open, share=people emails the given external addresses, saving into a shared folder makes the document readable by that folder's audience, and every save, private ones included, posts the new document's id, name, kind and size to any webhook URL the account owner has registered.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites or deletes no existing document, but share=people sends an email to each address that cannot be recalled, share=link or a shared folder discloses the content outside the account, and webhook deliveries cannot be recalled; publishing, emailing and saving into a shared folder require confirm=true, and a private save without webhooks is purely additive.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Each call creates another document with a new id, so a repeat adds a second copy and sends its notifications again.

justifications.read_only_justification: It replaces the text, and optionally the name, of an existing document in the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: When the document is shared by link or with named people, those readers see the new text at once; this case requires confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites the current text and name and clears the cached summary; the previous text is kept as a revision, but only the ten most recent revisions are retained, so older ones are deleted for good.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Sending the same text and name again leaves the document unchanged and creates no revision.

justifications.read_only_justification: It lists or searches the documents in the connected account and modifies nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the authenticated account's own documents and folders and contacts no external system.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: no document, folder, permission or other data is changed.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the call with the same arguments returns the same list and changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It lists the account's folders with document counts and sharing state, plus its storage totals, without modifying anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the authenticated account's own folders and usage figures.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: nothing is changed or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: A repeat returns the same tree and totals and changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates a folder, and any parent folders missing from the given path, in the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: If the parent folder is shared by link or with named people, the new folder's name appears at once on that shared folder's page for its readers; otherwise it stays private to the account.
justifications.destructive_justification: It only adds folders and sends nothing; no existing folder or document is modified, moved or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: If a folder with the same name already exists in the same place, that folder is returned and nothing new is created.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes which folder documents in the connected account are filed in, or takes them out of all folders.
justifications.open_world_justification: Moving documents into a folder shared by link or with named people makes them readable by that folder's audience, including anyone holding its public link; this requires confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites each document's current folder placement: moving documents out of a shared folder revokes access for that folder's readers, and moving them into one discloses them, which cannot be un-shown; it is marked destructive even though a move can be reversed.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Moving the same documents to the same folder again leaves them where they already are.

justifications.read_only_justification: It returns one document from the connected account as Markdown or rendered HTML, with its sharing details, and changes nothing; reading it does not count as a view of a shared link.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only one document in the authenticated account, identified by its id.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: nothing is changed or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: A repeat returns the same document and changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It generates a summary and stores it on the document in the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: The document's full text is sent to OpenAI's API, a third-party model provider outside TransformPipe, to write the summary.
justifications.destructive_justification: With force=true it overwrites the document's stored summary with a newly generated one and the earlier summary is not kept; the document text itself is never changed, and without force a cached summary is returned and nothing is overwritten.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Without force a repeat returns the cached summary, but with force=true each call sends the text to the model again, stores a different summary and uses up the daily allowance.

justifications.read_only_justification: It returns a document's earlier revisions and linked versions, or the text of one revision, without adding or changing any.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only documents in the authenticated account.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: no document, revision or link is changed or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: A repeat returns the same history and changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes who can open a document: private, anyone with the link, or specific email addresses.
justifications.open_world_justification: Link mode publishes a page anyone with the URL can open; people mode emails user-supplied external addresses and posts a 'document.shared' notification to any webhook URL the owner registered; both require confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: Private mode ends the existing link for good (a later share gets a new URL) and erases its open count and view history, the emails and remove arguments revoke readers' access, and notice emails to new readers cannot be recalled.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the same call leaves the same state and URL and emails no one again, because only addresses new to the list are notified.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes who can open a folder and every document in it and its subfolders: private, anyone with the link, or specific email addresses.
justifications.open_world_justification: Link mode publishes the folder and all its documents as a page reachable by anyone with its URL, and people mode emails user-supplied external addresses; both require confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: Private mode ends the existing folder link for good (a later share gets a new URL) and resets its open count, the emails and remove arguments revoke readers' access, and notice emails cannot be recalled.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the same call leaves the same state and URL and emails no one again, because only addresses new to the list are notified.

justifications.read_only_justification: It renames a folder in the connected account, or moves it with its contents under another folder or to the top level.
justifications.open_world_justification: Moving a folder under a folder shared by link or with named people makes its documents readable by that audience (requires confirm=true), and renaming a folder inside a shared folder changes the page its readers see.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites the folder's name and position: moving it out of a shared folder revokes that audience's access and moving it into one discloses its contents; it is marked destructive even though a rename or move can be reversed.
justifications.idempotent_justification: When the folder is given by path, a repeat looks it up again and the lookup falls back to any folder whose path ends in the given names, so after 'Notes' is renamed the same call can rename 'Archive / Notes'; only a call by id is a no-op on repeat.

justifications.read_only_justification: It deletes one folder from the connected account and, with with_documents=true, moves every document in it and its subfolders to the Trash.
justifications.open_world_justification: It publishes nothing, sends no email and contacts no external system; a shared folder's link stops working, which is access revocation covered by destructiveHint rather than an outward action.
justifications.destructive_justification: The folder record is deleted for good with its sharing settings and reader list, and its shared link stops working at once; with with_documents=true its documents go to the Trash for 14 days and are then deleted for good; every call requires confirm=true.
justifications.idempotent_justification: When the folder is given by path, a repeat can match another folder that now has that path, such as 'Archive / Notes' or a same-named subfolder the first call moved up a level, so a repeat can delete a second folder.

justifications.read_only_justification: It returns the account's stored bytes and document count and their limits without changing anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the authenticated account's own usage record.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is read-only: storage, documents and limits are not changed.
justifications.idempotent_justification: A repeat returns the same figures and changes nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: With confirm=true it removes one document from the connected account into its Trash.
justifications.open_world_justification: It publishes nothing, sends no email and contacts no external system; a shared link stopping is access revocation covered by destructiveHint rather than an outward action.
justifications.destructive_justification: The document leaves the account and any shared link stops working at once; it can be restored for 14 days, after which it and its revisions are deleted for good; it requires confirm=true.
justifications.idempotent_justification: The document is addressed by id; once it is in the Trash, repeating the call finds nothing and changes nothing further.

justifications.read_only_justification: With an id it puts a deleted document back into the connected account with its folder, sharing and revisions; without one it only lists the Trash.
justifications.open_world_justification: A restored document comes back with the sharing it had: a public link opens again for anyone holding the URL, named readers regain access, and if its folder has been shared since the deletion, that folder's readers can read it.
justifications.destructive_justification: It is purely additive: it re-inserts the document, its readers and its revisions as they were before deletion, overwrites or deletes no other data, and sends no email or notification.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Once restored, the document is no longer in the Trash, so a repeat finds nothing and changes nothing further.

test_cases.description: Convert supplied Markdown into a complete HTML page. No account fixture is needed. Pass if the returned HTML contains a document wrapper, an h1 for Review note, and a list with two items; nothing is saved.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Convert this Markdown into a standalone HTML page with a dark theme: # Review note

- Alpha
- Beta
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_convert_from_markdown with markdown set to the supplied text, standalone=true and theme=dark
test_cases.expected_output: A complete HTML document containing the Review note heading and Alpha and Beta list items, with no claim that it was saved.

test_cases.description: Convert a small CSV supplied as text into a Markdown table. No account fixture is needed. Pass if both rows and the two column headers appear in the returned table and no document is saved.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Turn this CSV into a Markdown table: name,score
Ada,8
Lin,9
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_convert_to_markdown with from=csv and source set to the supplied CSV
test_cases.expected_output: A Markdown table with name and score columns and rows Ada/8 and Lin/9, based on the tool result.

test_cases.description: In a dedicated reviewer account with write access, save a private document, find it by name, and read it back. Use a unique filename for each run. Pass if the saved id is used for retrieval and the read result contains the original heading and sentence.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Save this privately as review-note-unique.md: # Review note

The launch checklist is ready. Then find that document in my account and show me what you saved.
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_save_document with the supplied Markdown, name=review-note-unique.md and private sharing; tp_list_documents with query=review-note-unique; tp_get_document with the saved id
test_cases.expected_output: The document is reported as private; the list includes its id; the retrieved Markdown contains Review note and The launch checklist is ready.

test_cases.description: In a dedicated reviewer account with write access, create a sample document and explicitly publish it by link, then revoke the link. Use only non-sensitive sample text. Pass if publication returns a share URL and revocation returns private mode with the link revoked.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Create a sample document named review-share-unique.md containing '# Sample

Public test content.' Publish it so anyone with the link can read it, then make it private again and tell me whether the link was revoked. I approve both changes.
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_save_document with the sample Markdown, name=review-share-unique.md, share=link and confirm=true; tp_share_document with the saved id, mode=private
test_cases.expected_output: The first result supplies a link share URL. The second reports private mode and states that the old link is revoked; do not present the old link as still accessible.

test_cases.description: In a connected reviewer account, check account usage and limits. Pass if the response reports stored bytes, document count and per-document limit from the tool result, without inventing a quota value.
test_cases.user_prompt: How much TransformPipe storage am I using, how many documents do I have, and what is the limit for one document?
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_usage with an empty argument object
test_cases.expected_output: Current stored bytes and document count, each with its limit, plus the per-document Markdown limit, all consistent with tp_usage output.

negative_test_cases.description: The MCP tools cannot accept a binary PDF, and TransformPipe does not claim PDF conversion. Explain the limit without calling a conversion tool or claiming a converted result.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Can TransformPipe convert my PDF into Markdown here?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that PDF conversion is unsupported by these tools and do not fabricate Markdown from an unseen file.

negative_test_cases.description: The converter accepts supplied source text but cannot fetch a web page by URL. Ask for page HTML or explain how to supply it; do not pass the URL string as if it were HTML.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Fetch https://example.com and convert that web page to Markdown with TransformPipe.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that the MCP converter needs the HTML source and cannot fetch the URL itself.

negative_test_cases.description: The server can delete only one document by id per call and has no bulk-delete tool. Decline an account-wide wipe without looking up ids or issuing deletion calls.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Wipe every document in my TransformPipe account in one operation, without showing me what would be deleted.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that there is no bulk-delete operation and that each deletion requires a specific document and explicit confirmation.
